steps.text: Wet hands with running water; apply enough soap to cover all surfaces
Rub palms together, palm to palm
Rub right palm over left dorsum with interlaced fingers, then vice versa
Rub palm to palm with fingers interlaced
Rub back of fingers to opposing palms (fingers interlocked)
Rotational rubbing of right thumb clasped in left palm, then vice versa
Rotational rubbing of right fingertips in left palm, then vice versa
Rinse hands thoroughly under running water
Dry thoroughly with a single-use towel
Use towel to turn off faucet. Total duration: 40–60 seconds
Wash hands / apply gloves as appropriate
Explain procedure to patient and gain consent
Measure temperature (oral / axillary / tympanic)
Count radial pulse for 60 seconds, note rate, rhythm, volume
Count respirations for 60 seconds, note rate, depth, pattern
Measure blood pressure, correct cuff size, arm at heart level
Record SpO₂ with pulse oximeter
Assess pain using numeric or visual analogue scale
Record and document all findings accurately
Report any abnormal findings to senior staff immediately
Explain procedure; have patient rest quietly for ≥ 5 minutes
Patient seated, feet flat on floor, arm supported at heart level
Select correct cuff: bladder covers ≥ 80% of arm circumference
Apply cuff 2–3 cm above antecubital fossa
Locate brachial artery; place stethoscope bell/diaphragm over it
Inflate cuff 30 mmHg above point where radial pulse disappears
Deflate slowly at ~2 mmHg/sec; note Korotkoff Phase I (systolic)
Note Korotkoff Phase V, disappearance of sound (diastolic)
Fully deflate cuff. Wait ≥ 2 min before repeating
Record: reading, arm used, position, cuff size and time
Check prescription, 5 Rights: patient, drug, dose, route, time
Gather: correct gauge needle (21–23G, 2.5–3.8 cm), syringe, swab, gloves
Wash hands and apply gloves
Draw up medication using aseptic technique
Select site: deltoid / vastus lateralis / ventrogluteal / dorsogluteal
Clean site with 70% alcohol swab, allow to air-dry 30 seconds
Spread or bunch skin as appropriate for the muscle selected
Insert needle at 90° in one smooth motion
Aspirate 5–10 seconds, if blood appears, withdraw and restart
Inject slowly (~10 seconds per mL)
Withdraw needle at same angle; apply light pressure, do NOT rub
Dispose of needle in sharps bin immediately, do NOT re-cap
Document administration in medication record
Confirm prescription; explain procedure; gain informed consent
Prepare: cannula (correct gauge), tegaderm, tape, flush syringe
Select vein: antecubital, cephalic, basilic, or dorsal hand veins
Apply tourniquet 10 cm above selected site
Clean site with 2% chlorhexidine swab, allow to fully dry
Apply sterile gloves; stabilise vein with non-dominant hand
Insert cannula bevel-up at 10–30°; confirm flashback of blood
Lower angle, advance cannula off stylet, then withdraw stylet fully
Release tourniquet; apply finger pressure above cannula tip
Attach cap or extension set; flush with 5–10 mL normal saline
Secure with transparent dressing; label with date, time, gauge, initials
Document cannula insertion and site assessment in nursing notes
Review prescription; explain procedure to patient
Gather: sterile dressing pack, appropriate dressing, clean gloves, sterile gloves
Wash hands thoroughly; position patient comfortably
Open sterile pack using aseptic corners, maintain sterile field
Apply clean gloves; remove old dressing; observe and assess wound
Remove clean gloves; wash hands; apply sterile gloves
Irrigate wound with normal saline if required
Dry wound edges gently with sterile gauze
Apply appropriate dressing according to wound type
Secure dressing; label with date, time, nurse initials
Document wound assessment: size, depth, exudate, surrounding skin
Confirm prescription; explain procedure; gain informed consent
Gather: catheter pack, correct size catheter (12–14 Fr), sterile water for balloon
Position: supine with knees bent, legs apart, good light source
Wash hands; apply clean gloves; open sterile pack aseptically
Pour sterile saline/water; apply sterile gloves; place sterile drape
Cleanse labia majora front to back, discard each swab after single use
Cleanse labia minora front to back; then cleanse urethral meatus
Place sterile receiver between patient's legs
Insert lubricated catheter gently until urine flows; advance 5 cm further
Inflate balloon with prescribed volume of sterile water (usually 10 mL)
Gently withdraw catheter to confirm balloon is seated at bladder neck
Connect to drainage bag; secure catheter to inner thigh; document
Confirm prescription; explain procedure; gain consent
Gather: NGT (correct size), lubricant, pH strips, tape, drainage bag
Position: high Fowler's (45–90°) unless contraindicated
Check nostrils for obstruction, select wider nostril
Measure NEX (Nose–Earlobe–Xiphoid) for insertion length; mark tube
Wash hands, apply gloves; lubricate tube tip generously
Insert gently via nostril, aiming toward ear on same side
Ask patient to swallow as tube passes pharynx; advance to marked point
STOP immediately if resistance, coughing or respiratory distress
Confirm position: aspirate content; test pH, must be ≤ 5.5
Unconscious patients: confirm by chest X-ray before any use
Secure tube to nose with tape; document position confirmation method and length
Confirm prescription: O₂ flow rate, target SpO₂, delivery device
Assess baseline: SpO₂, respiratory rate, colour, consciousness
Select delivery device: nasal cannula / simple mask / non-rebreathe / Venturi
Check oxygen supply, cylinder level or wall outlet working
Set prescribed flow rate on flow meter
Apply device correctly to patient; check fit and comfort
Monitor SpO₂ continuously; document baseline and ongoing response
Titrate to target SpO₂: 94–98% adults; 88–92% COPD/hypercapnic patients
Reassess every 30 minutes or as per ward protocol
Document: device used, flow rate, SpO₂, RR, time and clinical response
Confirm frequency and prescription
Explain procedure to patient
Wash hands; apply clean gloves
Prepare glucometer, insert test strip; check expiry date
Warm patient's finger; clean with alcohol swab; allow to dry
Use lancet on side of fingertip, apply gentle pressure for blood drop
Apply blood to test strip, ensure adequate sample
Read and note result; note time and patient's last meal
Apply pressure to puncture site
Dispose of lancet and strip in sharps/clinical waste
Document result; report abnormal values immediately
